assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation resolves the horizon and flatness problems and, through quantum fluctuations of the inflaton, explains the origin of cosmic structure. This is one of the few ideas in theoretical cosmology that has reshaped the field and produced sharp, testable predictions: a nearly scale-invariant, adiabatic, Gaussian spectrum of perturbations. As a theorist who works on early-universe physics, I see this as the strongest conceptual advance on the list, and it is tied to measurements, not just to formal argument.
assessment.attribution: The decisive pieces are the inflationary mechanism (Guth, with Linde's new inflation and chaotic inflation fixing the graceful-exit problem) and the quantum origin of perturbations (Mukhanov, with Chibisov). The supplied credit supports a coherent three-person prize. Starobinsky's earlier contribution and the parallel work on fluctuations by others are not among the credited names, so the allocation is not clean and the committee would have to defend it.
assessment.maturity: The CMB acoustic peaks, the measured spectral tilt and the flatness of space from COBE, WMAP and Planck support the inflationary picture of perturbations. The simplest slow-roll predictions have held up. No primordial gravitational-wave signal has been seen, and inflation is not uniquely confirmed, so recognition is slightly early on the mechanism and well-founded on the observed perturbation spectrum.
uncertainties: Inflation is not uniquely established; alternatives to the standard paradigm remain, and primordial B-modes are undetected.
Credit is entangled with Starobinsky and others outside the supplied names.
I am working from my own knowledge of the history and have not verified priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators opened a new organising principle in condensed matter physics, and the experimental discovery in HgTe wells confirmed it. The discovery is conceptually clear and has had lasting influence on materials science and on the topological classification of phases.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical prediction and introduced the Z2 invariant. Molenkamp's group, in collaboration with the Zhang theory proposal, delivered the first observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal) and Fu and Kane (3D) are outside the supplied names, so the three-person configuration omits some important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Theory and experiment have been independently confirmed in several materials, including 3D topological insulators. The field is mature, stable and widely accepted. The recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction and for the three-dimensional generalisation is shared with people not on this entry.
Practical realisations remain limited, which does not affect the discovery itself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution connects the foundations of quantum mechanics (no-cloning, measurement disturbance) to a practical protocol with provable security. It is an original idea of clear conceptual value, and it has grown into the field of quantum cryptography with real experimental and commercial demonstrations.
assessment.attribution: BB84 by Bennett and Brassard is the clear origin of the field. Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol was an independent and conceptually important route, tied to Bell tests, but the first invention of QKD is best credited to Bennett and Brassard. I would propose these two and note the unresolved question of Ekert and, outside the supplied names, Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations over fibre and satellite links are well established, and security proofs are mature. The 2022 prize for entanglement experiments touched adjacent ground, so timing is reasonable, though a case can be made that this is more information science than physics.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards QKD as a physics discovery rather than an invention in information science.
Overlap with the 2022 prize and priority questions around Ekert and Wiesner.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP gave the first precision full-sky CMB maps and fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model to percent level: the age, the geometry, the matter and dark-energy content. It turned cosmology into a precision science. The discovery is an instrument-and-measurement achievement of major, durable influence.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was central to the instrument and the early experimental design, and Spergel to the analysis and cosmological interpretation. This is a defensible trio, but a mission with a large team and with Planck as a successor raises the usual question of who the decisive individuals are.
assessment.maturity: The results have been confirmed and refined by Planck and by other experiments. Maturity is not in doubt. The prior recognition of COBE and of dark energy reduces the novelty of the case relative to those prizes.
uncertainties: Attribution inside a large collaboration is difficult.
Part of the impact has already been recognised by earlier cosmology prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal showed how to build quantum gates with cold trapped ions, and trapped-ion experiments have since become a leading platform for quantum computation and simulation. The combination of a clear proposal and precise experiments is the type of concrete link between theory and nature I value.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the theoretical proposal; Blatt's group realised key gate and entanglement demonstrations at scale. Wineland's earlier work, already recognised in 2012, is outside the entry and overlaps with the experimental side, which could complicate allocation.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have replicated and extended the demonstrations, and the platform is mature. Whether the computing application is yet a stable scientific discovery is less clear, but the physics is secure.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with Wineland's contributions.
Entries B045 and B027 share Cirac and Zoller, so the committee must avoid inconsistent credit across candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: AdS/CFT is the most influential development in formal high-energy theory in decades. It gave a concrete non-perturbative formulation of quantum gravity in anti-de Sitter space and has informed black-hole information, entanglement and strongly coupled field theory. As someone from this field, I recognise its depth and also its limits.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena's 1997 conjecture is the origin; Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten supplied the dictionary soon after. The supplied credit is plausible, though others, such as Klebanov and Gubser (deceased), are outside the names.
assessment.maturity: There is no direct experimental confirmation, and the correspondence concerns anti-de Sitter space, not our universe. The Nobel Prize in Physics asks for discoveries in nature, and I would be cautious. Indirect support comes from consistency checks and from applications to heavy-ion physics, which are suggestive but not decisive.
uncertainties: No experimental test; relevance to our universe is unestablished.
The credit set omits several contributors.
Premature in the Nobel sense even though the idea is lasting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of magic-angle flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene, followed by the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity, created the field of moire quantum materials. It is a striking case where a theoretical prediction was borne out by a clear experiment and has opened a very large research area.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery. Cao, Fatemi and others who performed the experiments are not in the supplied names, so credit for the experiment is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have reproduced the phenomena, but the origin of superconductivity is still debated and the field is young. Timing is somewhat early, though the pace of confirmation is high.
uncertainties: Experimental credit extends beyond the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recognition that particles in two dimensions can have fractional exchange statistics is a deep conceptual discovery about quantum mechanics and topology. It is elegant, original and has lasting influence, especially in the fractional quantum Hall effect and topological quantum computing ideas.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim identified the possibility of intermediate statistics in 1977, and Wilczek named and developed anyons in 1982. This is a natural trio for the theory. Experimental confirmation belongs to a separate candidate, which suggests the parts may need different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Interferometry experiments in the fractional quantum Hall regime now give evidence of anyonic statistics, but non-Abelian anyons remain unconfirmed. Wilczek is already a laureate, which is not a barrier but is a consideration for the committee.
uncertainties: Whether to pair this with the experimental demonstration (B041) or treat them as separate.
Non-Abelian statistics are not yet demonstrated.
